text:
The Jets spent two months living inside the Connor Hellebuyck saga: a private trade request, a public one in August, a suspension for skipping camp, and finally the Oct. 23 trade to New Jersey for Dawson Mercer, Nico Daws, Nick Bjugstad, prospect Alexander Command and two picks. Hellebuyck said this week that threats against his family were behind it. Scott Arniel said Hellebuyck gave up on the team.

On the ice, the Jets are finally writing a new story. They have won five straight, outscoring teams 27-14, and the chances back it: 60% of the expected goals (the quality of chances for and against) in those games. That run came after a long October skid, so the season is still only 9-8-3 with 21 points, and our numbers have Winnipeg at 48% of the expected goals overall and a 31% chance at the playoffs.

Mercer has been exactly the piece they needed. He scored twice in the 4-2 win over the Devils in Hellebuyck's return and has 8 points in his last ten games (5.4 expected). Mark Scheifele tied the Jets' franchise points record in Thursday's 8-3 win in Dallas, and the Scheifele, Kyle Connor and Cole Perfetti line remains the engine. The power play creates 0.83 expected goals a game.

The concern is depth. Dylan DeMelo and Mario Ferraro have been outshot, and the goaltending without Hellebuyck has been roughly average. The rematch in New Jersey is Nov. 28.
headline: Life after Hellebuyck starts with five straight wins
